newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends firm on inflation hopes.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends firm on inflation hopes.

text.p: Mexican peso contracts closed firmer for the fifth consecutive session on Wednesday due to market optimism over imminent inflation data, traders said.
"Economic indicators look very good all round," a dealer said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate ended trade 1.65 and 1.6 centavos firmer, respectively, at 7.8840/7.8860 and 7.8820/7.8840 per dollar.
Banco de Mexico was expected to release inflation data for June shortly after the foreign exchange market closed.

A Reuters survey MEX22 of 13 Mexico City financial houses revealed they forecast an average rise of 0.9 percent for consumer prices in June. Same-day peso contracts closed earlier 2.0 centavos firmer at 7.8880/7.8910 per dollar.

Dealers said the peso may also have firmed due to banks switching from dollars to obtain liquidity to settle balances outstanding on checking accounts with the central bank. Wednesday was the central bank's monthly cutoff date for settlement.
Dealers added some banks may have taken advantage of a firm peso to exercise dollar put options previiously auctioned by the central bank.
"There were some puts left over, but not enough to have checked peso firmness. What's more, some dealers may even have exercised and gone short on dollars," one trader said
The trader estimated some $80 million in dollar puts had still to be exercised, out of $300 million auctioned at the end of last month.
Same-day peso contracts had previously closed 2.0 centavos firmer at 7.8880/7.8910.
Dealers said the market could open mixed on Thursday due to pre-weekend swaps.
